parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes universal, traveller-facing exposures: the federal document regime (no congruent markers, X-bar, mismatched papers triggering refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility) is in force and upheld, and the state bars birth-sex-incongruent facility use in schools and public buildings through a public complaint form whose defence requires in-state records a visitor lacks. Outed consequences are exclusion, forced outing, investigation and occasional arrest (trespass, up to 60 days; one documented custody placement in a men's ward), not likely imprisonment. Positives are real but partial: private venues exempt, no identity criminalisation, hate-crime and employment protections, partly enjoined federal orders, working courts. No state violence data exists. Net: Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order plus Feb 2025 rule: only M/F markers issued, X-marker processing halted, congruent markers refused; mismatch or doubt on sex triggers case refusal, and wilful-misrepresentation findings can support lifetime ineligibility. Travellers report confiscated or blocked passports and being stranded; eight foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; the restriction remains litigated by a civil-liberties union; a legal-aid FAQ tracks document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Border document doubt can escalate to refusal, adverse findings or secondary screening, then, once admitted, into the state's complaint-driven facility regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State trespass offence (up to 60 days) for willful entry plus refusal to leave a facility; one documented arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward. Complaint form triggers state investigation of reported trans people. Federal custody records show forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans detainees; federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No automatic arrest on entry; national hate-crime statute and employment protection apply; several federal orders are enjoined.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can move a visitor into federal custody where sex-assigned placement and hostile custody practice apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law (signed 30 Jan 2024) restricts restroom and locker-room use by sex assigned at birth in public schools and government buildings, enforced by official or private complaints via a public reporting form; the federal order separately bars congruent use of federally funded single-sex facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Law does not reach private businesses (hotels, gyms, commercial venues); new government buildings must include single-occupant facilities; offences require refusal to depart when asked.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding rules extend exposure into federally funded spaces the state law also covers, so a visitor in a capitol, museum or school tour carries continuous exposure.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors (signed 28 Jan 2023, immediate effect) with retroactive disaffirmance suits allowed up to age 25; proposed federal rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement under 18; the justice department subpoenaed pediatric gender-care records nationwide.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not banned in the state; clinicians may still treat under-25s; a commissioned review found the treatments effective and safe, though the legislature ignored it.
care_services.interaction: A family travelling with a trans minor faces care denial, possible insurer refusal and a liability shadow over any provider who treats the child.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State bans LGBTQ flags in schools and government buildings ($500/day fine) and its advocacy director calls it the national leader in anti-LGBTQ legislation; federal orders call care 'mutilation', direct investigation of schools, and a 2026 counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several federal orders are blocked or enjoined; the reward memo does not list gender ideology as a reward criterion; a major city adopted a trans-derived official flag.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing legitimises the complaint form, encouraging third-party reporting against visibly trans visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban for minors; 2024 dormitory exclusion for trans students; school facility rules by birth sex; an executive order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition, and the federal order rescinds name/pronoun recognition. A parent travelling with a trans child risks care denial and institutional outing.
minors_guardians.protection: Anti-bullying legislation since 2006; state conversion-therapy ban for minors (with clergy/parent exemptions); private venues and family lodging outside the facility law.
minors_guardians.interaction: School-adjacent exposure and the care ban combine so a visiting minor can be excluded, misnamed or denied treatment while the guardian attracts scrutiny.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific violence data was located; the public reporting form invites third-party complaints against visibly trans people in privacy spaces, and national statistics track only sexual-orientation bias counts.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute amended in 2019 to cover gender identity with enhanced penalties and mandatory statistics publication; 2015 employment and housing nondiscrimination statute.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absent public-accommodation protection, service refusals have no state remedy even where criminal bias offences apply.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The facilities-law defence requires an in-state birth certificate plus surgical proof a visitor will not carry, with no documented alternative for foreign or out-of-state documents; complaint volumes and outcomes are unrecorded; the state's status under national 'Do Not Travel' flags is unstated; document rules remain in litigation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Pending constitutional challenges, a running legal-aid FAQ, working state courts (marker changes granted by court order since 2021), and national employment and hate-crime protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Volatile, partly enjoined federal measures mean exposure at travel time is unpredictable and depends on which orders are operative.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far worse: fraud-based arrest with torture in custody, coerced confessions, closed judicial review and a plausible execution pathway. Here no custodial torture, likely imprisonment or capital exposure is documented, courts function and several federal measures are enjoined.

Lower than this case: birth-sex prison housing plus a cross-dressing offence reaching administrative buildings with remedies moving slowly. Our state criminalises only trespass after refusal to depart, private venues stay open, and hate-crime and employment protections operate — so this dossier sits above 0.25-C.

Closest fit: durable identity-document exposure reaching every service, hotel and database, administrative rather than custodial consequences, opaque slow remedies, no credible execution. Ours adds a criminal facility offence and a minor-care ban, holding it at or slightly below this level.

Materially safer: trained border officers, respectful inspection, brief detention with counsel, written reasons and compensation for unlawful holding. Our document regime deliberately restricts markers and contemplates lifetime ineligibility, with no such traveller-facing safeguards documented.

Well above this case: equality law covering gender identity in public services, chosen-name recognition, independent oversight delivering apologies and compensation. Our state lacks public-accommodation protection and operates an active birth-sex facility exclusion plus a citizen reporting channel.

parsed.synthesis: Federal and state layers compound rather than offset. Entry exposes the traveller first: congruent markers cannot be obtained, mismatches invite refusal and a possible lifetime fraud finding, and allied states now warn their citizens. Once admitted, the state's birth-sex facility rule and its anonymous reporting form create continuous, universal exposure in public buildings, while private venues remain open and no identity or sodomy offence exists. Severity peaks at arrest, sex-assigned short custody and service denial — not imprisonment or death. Protections are genuine (hate-crime statute, employment ruling, enjoined federal orders, working courts) but do not reach public accommodations, facilities or documents. For families, the minor-care ban, dormitory exclusion and school-investigation orders add a distinct layer of exposure.
